definition: A software system described as pursuing a task through model-guided decisions and actions. This atlas records the actual action and approval boundaries rather than assigning autonomy from the name.
The set of decisions and actions an agent may take without an additional human approval in a specified deployment.
An explicit decision that authorizes an action. Approval of a goal should be distinguished from approval of every possible means of pursuing it.
A manual action needed during a run. Record what the person did and whether the task could continue without it.
A named product that offers agent behavior. Its operator may also sell frameworks, infrastructure or non-agent products.
The organization or project responsible for providing a service. Product identity and legal-entity identity are separate fields.
Software used to construct agent behavior. The framework's documented features do not establish the behavior of every application built with it.
The environment that executes agent processes, tools and state transitions.
The surrounding system that supplies a model with tools, context, execution control and feedback for a task.
A callable operation made available to an agent, with defined inputs, outputs and possible side effects.
A machine-readable description of an operation's inputs and outputs. Validate the observed behavior separately.
The list of operations exposed by a particular service or deployment at a particular time.
An implementation that exposes capabilities through Model Context Protocol. It may run locally or be provided as a remote service.
A component that connects to MCP servers on behalf of a host application.
The application that contains or coordinates MCP client connections and presents capabilities to the user or model.
An MCP service whose tools retrieve documentation or reference material. Its existence does not establish access to the documented product's execution functions.
The mechanism carrying protocol messages between components. Record it alongside the protocol version and endpoint.
A network location at which a service is accessed. A homepage, registry listing and callable endpoint are different URL roles.
The process used to establish the identity of a caller or service.
The rules determining which actions an authenticated or anonymous caller is permitted to perform.
A bounded permission or area of access. Use the service's actual documented scope names when recording an integration.
The design practice of granting only the access needed for the intended task.
An authorization framework used to delegate access. The actual grant, scopes and token handling must be recorded for a specific integration.
A credential used to access an API. Its permissions, lifetime and organizational scope vary by service.
A credential or other sensitive value that should not appear in public profiles, logs or exported content.
An isolated or constrained environment used for execution or testing. Describe its actual boundaries instead of assuming complete isolation.
An operation that retrieves information. Reads can still expose sensitive data or incur charges.
An operation that changes state, such as editing a record, sending a message or submitting a transaction.
A property where repeating the same operation has the same intended effect as performing it once. Verify the service's documented mechanism.
A repeated attempt after a failure or uncertain result. Retries can create duplicate side effects if the workflow lacks appropriate controls.
Information maintained across steps or sessions, including task progress and stored context.
Information retained for future use by an agent. Evaluate retention, retrieval, correction and deletion separately.
The amount of input and generated content a model can consider within a particular interaction, subject to the model's limits.
A reusable set of instructions and resources for a class of tasks. In the Agent Skills format, the package centers on SKILL.md.
A collection of skills. Record individual paths and revisions when making claims about a specific skill.
An action or function a system is documented or observed to support. A capability is not a guarantee of task success.
A bounded request with inputs, constraints and an expected outcome.
The artifact or result submitted for evaluation, such as a patch, report, structured dataset or completed fixture record.
An observable condition used to decide whether a deliverable satisfies the task.
A controlled input and environment used to test behavior reproducibly.
A defined evaluation set and scoring method. Scores need version, settings and methodology to be comparable.
A process for measuring output or behavior against a stated rubric or expected result.
A record of execution events, such as model calls, tool calls and intermediate results, subject to the logging system's coverage.
The ability to inspect system behavior through traces, logs, metrics and related evidence.
A statement made by a product's operator. It should remain attributed until independently corroborated or tested.
An executed check against a specific version and environment. A documentation review is not a runtime test.
A scoped security assessment with identified methods and coverage. This package contains no new security-audit results.
Information describing where a statement or artifact came from and how it was obtained.
A structured source observation linked to one or more claims, with retrieval time and scope.
The date a source or behavior was inspected. It differs from publication date and the date an event occurred.
A field for which the research has not established a value. Unknown is different from unsupported, absent or false.
A capability explicitly documented or tested as not available in a specified scope. Do not use this label merely because evidence is missing.
A collection of structured identities or service records. Registration does not itself establish quality or trustworthiness.
A collection of listings intended for discovery. Directory records may require independent identity and freshness checks.
An A2A discovery document describing an agent's identity, advertised skills and interaction requirements.
Agent2Agent, a protocol for agent communication and task coordination.
Several unrelated protocols use ACP. Always expand the name and identify the ecosystem before comparing implementations.
A representation of authority to make a payment within stated conditions. Its format and enforcement depend on the implementation.
In an agent-payment context, a service that assists payment verification or settlement. Record its exact role for the protocol in use.
The completion of the relevant payment transfer. Settlement evidence does not establish that useful work was delivered.
An arrangement that holds funds subject to specified release conditions. Record who controls acceptance, expiry and disputes.
The party deciding whether submitted work meets the required conditions. The evaluator may or may not be independent of the client or provider.
Recorded feedback or signals about past behavior. Interpret the source, incentives, identity linkage and susceptibility to manipulation.
Software or a service used to manage signing or transaction authority. Custody, recovery and spending controls differ across implementations.
A constraint on payment authority, such as an amount, recipient, asset, time period or transaction class.
A testing network. A testnet transaction should not be presented as production revenue or production settlement.
Total attributable cost divided by the number of tasks that met the acceptance rubric. Include retries and human review where measured.
Pricing linked to a vendor-defined outcome. Compare the contractual definition of an outcome before comparing headline prices.
Pricing tied to a consumption unit, such as credits, tokens, calls or execution time. Units are not necessarily comparable across vendors.
Bring your own key: the customer supplies credentials for an underlying provider. Model or infrastructure charges may remain separate.
Terms governing use of a particular codebase or version. A repository license need not apply to a hosted service.
The atlas record representing one resolved entity. Aliases and registry listings can point to that record without becoming duplicate companies.
How recently a fact was checked relative to how quickly it can change. Prices and endpoints often need more frequent review than historical announcements.
A page the publisher intends search engines to consider for indexing. This is an implementation choice, not a promise of inclusion.
A concise passage that directly answers a specific reader question and links to supporting evidence.
A conclusion drawn from evidence rather than explicitly stated by a source. It must be labeled and kept separate from observed facts.
